opinions.item: Exact two owned sleeve-attached mitten hands
opinions.evaluation: Both existing coral quilted mittens remain continuously attached to the same cream sleeves and teal cuffs. No added arm, bare fingers, floating hand or outside operator appears.

opinions.item: Complete opaque gold cover of the one sweet
opinions.evaluation: The prior exposed red crescent is completely hidden by the attached opaque gold flap. One small oval covered volume remains in the same central tabletop task area; no second foreground sweet appears. This judges the depicted endpoint, not a proven folding span.

The screen-left rounded mitten rests against the left top of the covered oval; the screen-right thumb/palm braces the right free fold edge. Both contacts read as purposeful pressing rather than hands floating over an unrelated prop.

opinions.item: Conserved sweet scale and table registration
opinions.evaluation: The covered oval visually agrees with the prior small red sweet footprint and support. The broad lavender table, source framing, character size and scene registration remain coherent. Internal contents are inferred from the prior state; source stills do not establish temporal conservation.

opinions.item: Continuous attached sheet and next-step access
opinions.evaluation: The gold cover remains part of the same wide tabletop sheet with open side material. Neck pinches, opposite end twists and release have not occurred and must receive their own states and action review.

opinions.item: Specific wrapper material and painted style
opinions.evaluation: The authored crinkled gold surface, warm satin painted bands and plum contours are retained. It matches the commissioned gold-paper/red-sweet family; no plastic bag, string, detached ribbon or vector replacement is introduced. Dense original crease highlights remain an inclusive refinement priority.

Face, shell-trimmed teal cap, coral bows, brown hair/rainbow ribbon and costume remain recognizable. The lowered head attends to the tabletop group. A still cannot validate gaze through the complete performance.
The worktop still contains exactly one supported working object and its attached gold sheet. The removed foreground jars, bowls and utensils have not returned.

The same painted factory remains dense with distant metallic trim and small colored sweets. Preserving it avoids an unrelated redesign, but the inherited background hierarchy remains weak; no current runtime backdrop acceptance is claimed.

Provisional still floor: complete visible cover, two owned contacting mittens, conserved supported task and established style. Full fold trajectory, release, neck pinches, twists, ordinary game/training fit and owner acceptance remain open.
